newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly, Neurocrine in R&D accord - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly, Neurocrine in R&D accord - WSJ.

text.p: Neurocrine Biosciences Inc and drug manufacturer Eli Lilly & Co are expected to announce on Monday an agreement under which Neurocrine will get up to $74 million to develop new drugs for obesity and Alzheimer's disease, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The newspaper said in its Monday edition that Neurocrine would get the financial and scientific support for the new compounds that it was testing to treat the two diseases.
Under the five-year agreement with Lilly, Neurocrine will get $22 million in initial fees and funding, including $10 million during the first year, it said.

The newspaper said the remaining amount will be linked to the milestones that it will reach in development and regulation, adding that profits from U.S. sales of any drug resulting from the all-cash agreement will be shared.
"We get a very respectable percent of it that satisfies our criteria to participate significantly in the upside," it cited Gary Lyons, the company's president and chief executive officer, as saying.
Neurocrine will get royalties on any product sales outside the United States, it said.
